A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Federated ADMM from Bayesian Duality. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including matching renamed methods and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression and outlier experiments in Figures 3–4 and federated neural-network results in Tables 1–2, although some baseline results are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds IVON-PVI comparisons and hyperparameter sensitivity results in Figure 5 and Appendix J.

M1.justification: The BayesADMM updates, diagonal and full-covariance variants, IVON subroutine and tempered objective are retained. IVON-ADMM renames v1’s existing implementation. IVON-PVI experimentally instantiates a PVI specialization already described algebraically in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and the same illustrative regression/outlier scenarios. Homogeneous FashionMNIST results move from v1 Table 1 to v2 Table 4. New ablations use the existing heterogeneous CIFAR-100 task.

E2.justification: v2 adds IVON-PVI as an evaluated comparator on ResNet-20/CIFAR-100 in Figure 5 and Table 5; v1’s PVI comparison used the logistic-regression illustration. Main tables also combine the previously separate FedAvg and FedProx rows under one label.

E3.justification: New CIFAR-100 protocols vary temperature from 0.02 to 1 and inverse client step size from 0.1 to 5, and evaluate IVON-PVI with alpha=rho=1 and tuned dual damping. v2’s reporting description also drops v1’s explicit averaging over three preceding rounds; unchanged retained scores do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the illustrative analyses, v2 adds an IVON-PVI control that tests the contribution of the ADMM updates while retaining IVON, plus separate temperature and client-step-size sensitivity studies. Figure 5 and Tables 5–7 substantially expand evidence about convergence, tuning and instability.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three runs/seeds. The new ablation tables extend this existing practice; no increased run count, new confidence-interval procedure or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: Original proposed-method table scores are retained, but Figure 5 and Tables 5–7 add substantial results. Table 5 reports IVON-PVI versus IVON-ADMM accuracy of 31.5% versus 40.0% at 25 rounds and 47.5% versus 46.6% at 100 rounds. Sensitivity tables add divergent settings and temperature-dependent outcomes. Some separate baseline score series disappear through FedAvg/FedProx consolidation.

T1.justification: Both propositions and their proofs are retained. v2 corrects Table 3’s Gaussian natural parameters from m to sm/Sm and corrects the delta-approximation expression. It adds explicit derivation steps, but the new Appendix A dual-step argmax has a positive quadratic and is unbounded as written.

C1.justification: v2 qualifies the headline recovery claim: isotropic Gaussians yield ADMM-like updates, and classical ADMM additionally requires the delta approximation. That condition already appeared in v1’s technical discussion. The central Bayesian-duality contribution, quadratic one-round convergence and approximately 7% accuracy-improvement claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes faster early convergence from comparable final accuracy against IVON-PVI and explains temperature sensitivity and the stability–accuracy tradeoff in client step size. It removes v1’s explicit consensus-only and diagonal-covariance limitations, as well as the interpretation that low NLL demonstrates absence of overfitting. These materially revise the discussion of strengths and boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies approximately 250,000 ResNet-20 parameters, no CIFAR-100 data augmentation, and the reference client step size of 0.5. These are disclosures rather than established changes to existing experiments. Conversely, v1’s code-access link is absent from v2.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Ma et al. on Bregman Douglas-Rachford splitting, Opper and Winther on expectation-consistent inference, and Xu et al. on adaptive ADMM. It removes the federated SAM references by Fan et al. and Qu et al. The central positioning relative to PVI, AMA and ADMM remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and theoretical narrative are extensively rewritten. Section 3 separates VB background, Bayesian duality and BayesADMM; appendices reorganize the earlier material into additional dedicated sections. Terminology changes to IVON-ADMM, citations switch to author–year style, and an author affiliation changes.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the experimental displays: Tables 1–2 share a page, homogeneous FashionMNIST moves to Table 4, and FedAvg/FedProx rows merge. It adds Figure 5 and three ablation tables, restyles Figure 4’s markers, and changes document typography and layout.

improvement.justification: The new IVON-PVI control and sensitivity studies improve empirical support by distinguishing early convergence advantages from final accuracy and exposing unstable settings. This provides a limited net gain, tempered by less transparent merged baseline reporting, removal of the code link and explicit scope limitations, and a local error in the added dual-step derivation. The central method, proofs and original proposed-method benchmark scores remain largely unchanged.
